Quick context: Acme (our pilot) has asked whether we can support a migration from Zendesk to Intercom for their support surface. They want to know impact on routing, embedding search relevance (Console + embeddings), and how the CS stack will work with Gainsight for health scoring. Acme is also asking for a cost comparison and timeline before next-week exec sync.

I attached an initial cost spreadsheet and a short checklist (intercom-integration-checklist.pdf). Can each of you weigh in on the items below by EOD tomorrow so I can prep the exec slide: 

- Monica: high-level licensing delta (Zendesk -> Intercom), any volume breakpoints we should flag
- Marissa: Gainsight connector implications (events, identity mapping, retention) and whether we need an additional paid connector
- Laura: procurement/budget constraints and whether we can re-use the current Zendesk credits or need a fresh contract
- Diego: any infra/security blockers (data residency, webhook signing, audit logs)

Attachments: migration-costs-vs-zendesk.xlsx; intercom-integration-checklist.pdf

Jordan —

Thanks for the doc. Quick notes: Intercom licensing model is more seat/MAU oriented versus Zendesk's tiered agent model. For Acme's volume (estimated 120k MAU, ~25 agents), expect roughly a 20-30% lift vs current Zendesk list price unless we negotiate volume credits. See the top sheet in the attached workbook for a quick calc I did (tab: licensing-estimate).

Routing: Intercom's rules engine can handle most of our routing needs but we'll lose a few out-of-the-box Zendesk macros that Acme currently uses. We should confirm whether Acme needs advanced triggers that require Intercom's higher-tier product.

I'll loop in Carlos at Intercom to get an official quote and a feature matrix.

-Monica

Hi Jordan / Monica —

Thanks for reaching out. Happy to help. A few quick answers:

- Feature matrix: Intercom supports conversation routing, bots, and a flexible events API that can push to Gainsight and custom backends. I attached our public feature matrix and a short note on GDPR controls.
- Pricing: For enterprise MAU counts, we typically offer tiered pricing with a committed MAU discount. I can put together a formal quote once we confirm expected MAU and needed features (workflows, help center, bots).
- Data export / retention: We support export of conversation history and event streams (webhooks + batch exports). If you require historical migration (Zendesk tickets -> Intercom conversations), we can run a migration service (one-time fee).

Can we schedule a 45-minute technical deep-dive on Thursday 10/08 or Friday 10/09? I'll bring our integration engineer to walk through webhooks, event schema, and recommended migration approach.

Jordan / team —

High-level from CS / Gainsight perspective:

- Gainsight connector: Gainsight can consume Intercom events (conversations, user events) via the Intercom-to-Gainsight connector, but the mapping isn't 1:1 for some ticket fields we currently use (custom fields + macro histories). We'll need a transformation layer or rely on webhooks -> ingestion pipeline. There is an enterprise connector (paid) that covers some heavy lifting.
- Health scoring: If we lose ticket-level granularities (e.g., macro usage metrics), we should identify surrogate signals (response time, reopened convs, NPS events) so scoring doesn't degrade.
- Timeline: For a pilot (Acme size) assume 6-8 weeks including migration of ~18 months of ticket history (if they want it). Full-scale migration + connectors = 10-12 weeks.

I'm copying Nina from Gainsight (below) to validate connector details and cost. Also attaching a draft SOW outline that Procurement can use as a starting point (sow-draft-v1.docx).

-Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success | Redwood Inference

Thanks for the ping. Quick confirmation: Gainsight does offer a certified Intercom connector as part of our Enterprise Connectors suite. Notes:

- Connector capabilities: user-level events, conversation metadata, custom event mapping. Historical backfill is possible but will be scoped as a professional services engagement.
- Pricing: Connector licensing starts at $25k/year for Enterprise tier customers; historical backfill / mapping work is quoted separately (typical PS engagement $8k-$20k depending on volume and complexity).
- Data retention & PII: We support field-level redaction and can route PII to a separate storage bucket if required.
